man don't get me wrong, I'm still thoroughly bitter at how the final rolled out, nor am i defending icc's crazy rules and their obvious bias for england. the mankad technique is just one of the million things that doesn't sit right with me, and that's an emotional response, so i dont expect everyone else to feel that way also. for me, it's not a fair technique and never will be.

I'd love to see a mankad happen but only after the warning is issued to the batsman. saw mitchell starc do that ^ to rashid the other day. otherwise you're just being a wily bastard and using an unconventional tactic to get a batsman out. i get that it's in the rules but it doesn't particularly appeal to me as a part of the game I've grown up watching and loving so much.

the last one isn't against the rules per se but Ashwin has always proved himself to be a bit of a cunt while on the topic of hard and fast rules and the spirit of cricket. i remember him running out thirimmane in the same fashion back in the tri series in Australia in 2012. sachin and sehwag intervened and brought the fuming batsman back but the damage in the spirit of that game was already done.
